newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chronology of events in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of events in Chechnya.

text.p: The inauguration of new Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov is the latest stage of an independence struggle in the Caucasus region that dates back to Russian wars of conquest in the 19th century.
Here is a history of the region and of the two-year conflict that began when troops were sent there by Russia to crush an independence bid.
1859 - The Moslem North Caucasus region of Chechnya is incorporated into the Russian empire after nearly half a century of fighting led by legendary Imam Shamil.
1870 - The regional capital Grozny is founded.
1944 - Soviet dictator Josef Stalin deports the entire Chechen people to Central Asia, accusing them of collaboration with Nazi Germany. Tens of thousands die.
1957 - Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev allows the Chechens back to the Caucasus, where the Checheno-Ingush ethnic republic is set up.
Oct 1991 - Following the overthrow of local communist ruler Doku Zavgayev, Soviet air force general Dzhokhar Dudayev wins a disputed local poll and declares Chechnya independent.
Nov 1991 - Russian President Boris Yeltsin declares a state of emergency in the territory and sends troops to Chechnya. They pull out after a few hours.

Summer/Autumn 1994 - Russia says Dudayev is letting Chechnya become a haven for terrorists and urges the Chechens to topple him. Moscow gives covert military support to the anti-Dudayev opposition but an armed assault on Grozny fails.
Dec 1994 - President Boris Yeltsin sends troops to Chechnya to crush Dudayev's independence movement, but they meet strong resistance from local guerrilla fighters and suffer heavy casualties.
Jan 1995 - Russian troops start storming Grozny after tank, artillery and rocket attacks have reduced much of it to ruins.
Feb 1995 - Separatists abandon Grozny.
March 1995 - The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) sets up a mission in Chechnya.

June 1995 - About 100 rebels, led by guerrilla commander Shamil Basayev, storm the southern Russian town of Budennovsk and seize hundreds of hostages in a raid in which scores of people are killed. Peace talks open and Russia orders a halt to military operations in Chechnya. But the conflict goes on.
Dec 1995 - Russian-backed leader Zavgayev wins an election to head Chechnya's administration, but there are widespread reports of electoral fraud.

Jan 1996 - Fighters led by Salman Raduyev seize hostages in neighbouring Dagestan, then move to the village of Pervomaiskoye just outside Chechnya. Most rebels escape after a four-day stand-off with Russian troops but scores are killed.
Feb 1996 - Yeltsin says the Chechnya campaign was "maybe one of our mistakes". He says he is studying options for peace but rules out withdrawal of Russian forces or massive use of force.

March 1996 - Rebels attack Grozny and hold some areas for several days. Yeltsin announces a halt to wide-scale military action, a partial withdrawal of troops and an offer of indirect talks with the rebels. But the fighting continues.
April 1996 - Dudayev is reported killed in a rocket attack and replaced by vice-president Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev.
May 1996 - Yeltsin and Yandarbiyev agree a truce at talks in Moscow. It holds until the presidential poll which Yeltsin wins some six weeks later. Yeltsin visits Russian troops in Grozny.
Aug 1996 - Chechen rebels infiltrate Grozny and seize the city.

Yeltsin gives national security adviser Alexander Lebed powers to resolve the crisis. Lebed signs a peace deal on August 31 providing for a Russian troop pullout and deferring the issue of Chechen sovereignty for five years.
Sept 1996 - Russia starts withdrawing its soldiers.

Oct 1996 - Aslan Maskhadov, rebel chief-of-staff during the fighting, is named prime minister of an interim government pending January elections. His platform includes independence and introducing some elements of Islamic sharia law.
Dec 1996 - Six Red Cross workers are murdered in Chechnya, casting a shadow over the presidential election campaign.
Jan 1997 - Thirteen candidates run for president on January 27 and Maskhadov is elected with almost 65 percent of the vote. The OSCE says the poll was fair.
Feb 12, 1997 - Maskhadov takes his oath of office.
